newsitem.title: USA: Sales tax rebates up for Texas cities and counties.
newsitem.headline: Sales tax rebates up for Texas cities and counties.

text.p: The Texas comptroller of public accounts last week delivered a total of $151.2 million in monthly sales tax payments to the state's cities and counties, a 5.3 percent increase over March 1996 payments.

"Sales tax rebates to Texas cities and counties are 6.4 percent higher for the first three months of 1997 than for the same period last year, as consumers continue to show their confidence in a healthy Texas economy," State Comptroller John Sharp said in a release.
This month's sales payments include sales taxes collected in January, and reported by businesses filing returns in February.
Sales tax rebates to 1,086 Texas cities totaled $137.8 million, a 5.3 percent increase compared to last year's March payments of $130.8 million.
Rebates of totaling $13.3 million to 117 Texas counties were "virtually unchanged" from county allocations in March 1996, the release said.
